name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Quigley with large cash advantage
Republican challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Quigley holds a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat with a large financial edge, while Hanson shows no measurable campaign infrastructure. Fundamentals and markets both point to an easy incumbent win.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Mike Quigley seeks another term in a Chicago-area district that leans Democratic by about nineteen points. He has raised over $700,000 and holds more than $1.1 million on hand, while Republican Tommy Hanson reports no fundraising or cash on hand and draws no outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent. The seat's strong partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the challenger's minimal operation all point the same direction. Quigley is a heavy favorite to return to Congress, with the main uncertainty being the size of his victory margin rather than the outcome itself.
